2610.07580.title: LOGIC: An LLM Benchmark for Intent-Grounded Change Impact in Aerospace Electrical Systems
2610.07580.paper_summary: Aerospace electrical-design revisions can contain multiple genuine changes, although an engineering request may authorize only a subset. Propagating every detected difference can therefore produce overly broad impact reports. We present LOGIC, a controlled benchmark and evaluation framework in which locally deployable language models ground a request in a deterministic candidate-change inventory before selected changes are propagated through a typed electrical traceability graph. This separation permits candidate-selection errors to be distinguished from downstream propagation errors. LOGIC contains 168 scenarios, including 144 selection and 24 abstention cases. We evaluate three 7--8B models against intent-agnostic, lexical, and structured-evidence methods, with an oracle-root upper bound. On 96 explicitly anchored selection cases, gate-only structured evidence achieves candidate F1 of 1.0000, compared with 0.9677 for token-lexical matching. On 12 relational-paraphrase cases, token-lexical F1 is 0.1772 and gate-only F1 is 0.0000, compared with 0.5000--0.6400 for the large language models. Model grounding degrades as candidate inventories grow from 4 to 64 changes, while affected-element and typed-path accuracy remain comparatively stable when frozen selections are replayed over graphs of approximately 1K to 100K nodes. Strict evidence gating suppresses false positives but can remove correct semantic selections. An exploratory evidence-empty abstention policy raises strict abstention accuracy to 0.6667 for all three models and reduces unsafe-report rates to 0.1667, while decreasing answerable-case coverage by 16.0--27.1 percentage points. Four of six conflicting requests remain unsafe for each model. These findings support combining literal evidence and language-model reasoning with engineering review when intent cannot be established reliably.
2610.07580.paper_summary_zh: 航空電子設計的修訂可能包含多個真實變更，儘管工程請求可能僅授權子集。因此，傳播每個檢測到的差異可能會產生過於廣泛的影響報告。我們提出了LOGIC，一個受控的基準和評估框架，在該框架中，本地可部署的語言模型將請求基於確定性的候選變更庫進行基礎，然後選定的變更通過類型化的電子可追溯性圖進行傳播。這種分離允許將候選選擇錯誤與下游傳播錯誤區分開來。LOGIC包含168個場景，包括144個選擇案例和24個放棄案例。我們評估了三個7-8B模型，與無意圖、詞彙和結構證據方法進行比較，並設置了oracle-root的上限。在96個明確固定的選擇案例中，僅門控的結構證據達到候選F1為1.0000，而令牌-詞彙匹配的F1為0.9677。在12個關係-釋義案例中，令牌-詞彙的F1為0.1772，僅門控的F1為0.0000，而大型語言模型的F1為0.5000-0.6400。隨著候選庫從4個變更增長到64個變更，模型基礎的性能下降，而當固定選擇在約1K到100K節點的圖上重播時，受影響元素和類型路徑的準確性保持相對穩定。嚴格的證據門控抑制了假陽性，但可能會移除正確的語義選擇。一項探索性的證據空白放棄政策將所有三個模型的嚴格放棄準確率提高到0.6667，並將不安全報告率降低到0.1667，同時使可回答案例的覆蓋率下降了16.0-27.1個百分點。六個衝突請求中有四個對每個模型仍然是不安全的。這些發現支持在無法可靠建立意圖時，將字面證據和語言模型推理與工程審查相結合。
